chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
It was said to him: 'And what is the originating lie?'
He said: 'That a man narrates a hadith to you, and you leave him and report it from the one from whom he had narrated it.'

key_terms.إِيَّاكُمْ: Beware — emphatic second-person warning formula (إِيَّاكُمْ وَ...) characteristic of Imamic exhortations
key_terms.الْكَذِبُ الْمُفْتَرِعُ: The originating/branching lie — a term unique to hadith sciences denoting the falsification of the isnad by omitting a direct narrator and attributing the narration to a higher source

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about skipping a narrator in a hadith chain in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies and prohibits a subtle form of falsification in hadith transmission: a student who receives a narration directly from a teacher then reports it as though he received it from the teacher's own source, thereby erasing one link in the isnad. This is deemed a 'lie' because it deliberately misrepresents the transmission chain, potentially inflating the narration's apparent authority by skipping a less-known or less-reliable intermediate.
word_analysis: he narrates a hadith to you

en.hubeali: And by this chain, from Muhammad Bin Ali, raising it, said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Beware of the branched out lie!’
It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘And what is the branched out lie?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man narrates to you a Hadeeth, so you neglect him and report it from the person from whom he had narrated the Hadeeth.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated through the same chain of narrators from Muhammad ibn Ali in a marfu‘ manner from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said,
They asked the Imam, “What is branched-out lies?”
The Imam replied, “It is when a person narrates a Hadith to you and you would ignore him and narrate it from the person from whom he had narrated the Hadith.’”
